moments.selftext: Metallica’s new multimillion-dollar foundation funds trade school across the U.S. It has let tens of thousands of people gain skills without crushing debt. Metallica is famous for heavy metal. For several years the band has also been quietly financing training. Through its nonprofit, All Within My Hands, it has committed more than $17 million to trade programs in the United States. A 2019 pilot at ten community colleges grew into the Metallica Scholars Initiative. By mid-2026 the program reached students at 93 community colleges in all 50 states and Guam. It has helped tens of thousands of people learn high-demand trades without taking on debt. The money supports hands-on programs such as welding, advanced manufacturing, health care, automotive repair, and firefighting. Besides tuition, the foundation pays for safety gear, course materials, and basics such as transportation so students can finish. Band members, including James Hetfield, have said they take pride in raising the standing of trade work and in careers that can support a family. In 2026 the initiative made its first international grant, in the United Kingdom. The band is as serious about the workforce as it is about the stage. [All Within My Hands. (2026). Metallica Scholars Initiative National Workforce Education Program Expands to Over 90 Schools. All Within My Hands Foundation]

moments.selftext: Peter Cullen, the legendary voice behind Optimus Prime and countless other beloved characters, has died at the age of 85. Born in Montreal in 1941, Cullen began his career in Canadian radio and television before becoming one of the most recognizable voices in animation. He first voiced Optimus Prime in the original Transformers series in 1984, basing the character’s calm, commanding voice on his older brother Larry, a Marine veteran who taught him that a true hero should be “strong enough to be gentle.” Cullen returned to the role for more than four decades, including the live-action Transformers films beginning in 2007. His remarkable range extended far beyond Optimus. Cullen voiced Eeyore in numerous Winnie the Pooh productions, KARR in Knight Rider, and characters in G.I. Joe, Voltron, Chip ’n Dale Rescue Rangers, and countless other productions. He also created the distinctive vocal sounds of the alien hunter in Predator. In 2023, Cullen received a Lifetime Achievement Award at the Children’s & Family Emmy Awards, honoring a voice-acting career that spanned more than half a century. He died at his Los Angeles home on August 26, 2026, surrounded by his family.

moments.selftext: To be happy, you must eliminate two things: the fear of a bad future and the memory of a bad past. - Seneca Seneca (4 BC–65 AD), the Roman Stoic philosopher and advisor to Emperor Nero, believed that much of human suffering is self-inflicted. In Letters to Lucilius, he wrote, “we suffer more often in imagination than in reality,” suggesting that fear of future misfortune often causes more distress than the misfortune itself. To Seneca, anxiety over what might happen reflected a failure to accept fate and the natural order. The Stoics taught that events beyond our control should be met with calm and reason. What matters is not always what happens, but how we choose to respond. Seneca also warned against becoming prisoners of the past. In On the Shortness of Life, he argued that people waste their limited time by dwelling on what has already happened or constantly worrying about what comes next. The past is fixed and beyond our control, and repeatedly reliving it through regret or resentment only takes us further away from the present. This did not mean forgetting the past or abandoning plans for the future. Rather, Seneca believed that becoming emotionally trapped by past suffering or future fears robs us of tranquility. His philosophy emphasized living according to reason, accepting mortality, and recognizing time as our most valuable possession. For Seneca, freedom from fear and regret was not indifference. It was the ability to master our thoughts, focus on the present, and remain in control of our response to whatever life brings.
